newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa public sector Q3 worker numbers edge up.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa public sector Q3 worker numbers edge up.

text.p: The total number of workers in South Africa's public sector rose marginally by 0.2 percent in the three months from June to September 1996, the Central Statistical Service said Thursday.
The CSS said in a statement 4,675 workers swelled the state ranks to 1,923,354 and the greatest increase had been at local council level, where numbers grew 1.9 percent or 4,465 workers.
Provincial authorities showed a 0.3 percent rise and public corporation staff numbers went up 0.1 percent.
But the CSS said the number of employees in national departments decreased by 0.2 percent or 944 workers from the previous quarter to 597,251.
Declines were also reported in parastatals (2.1 percent), universities and technikons (polytechnics) (0.3) and agricultural marketing boards (2.3).
Year on year the total number of employees in the public sector increased by 2.8 percent or 52,092 workers to over 1.92 million workers from September 1995's 1.87 million, the CSS said.
South Africa's macro-economic plan, unveiled by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel last June, called for a programme of trimming state staff numbers.
After interim increases to fund the lay-offs, the plan, which maps the country's five-year economic plan, stipulates a reduction in the state's overall wage bill.
